stories.headline: Tencent says a new US chip rule sets China back; Jefferies sees a $44B to $62B hit to Nvidia
stories.dek: Nvidia has stopped H200 sales in China, and its $130B forecast for this quarter assumes no China data center chip revenue.

facts.text: Commerce issued a rule so chip export limits can't be bypassed through remote access to data centers in third countries
president Martin Lau said the rule "sets everyone back in China" and leaves Tencent unable to offer high-end GPUs in its cloud outside China
Jefferies' estimate of the rule's hit to next year's data center revenue; acting CEO Colette Kress says backlog means no top-line impact
Nvidia's revenue outlook for this quarter, plus or minus 3%, assuming no data center compute revenue from China, where it has stopped selling H200 chips

open.label: Open question
open.text: How much demand is tied to China. Critics put it as high as 20% of revenue, and Nvidia stopped disclosing its Singapore subsidiary's revenue after it hit $104B in 2025.

chart.note: Derived: Q3 data center revenue of $107.6B times four. Jefferies' range is for next year.

stories.headline: Officials say the outages weren't attacks; AI helped find flaws in Nginx, used on 56.7M hosts
stories.dek: Officials pointed to maintenance and technical changes. A critical new Nginx bug means another round of urgent patching.

facts.text: the DNI, the DHS secretary and the FBI's deputy director told a House hearing they found no sign the outages were linked or were attacks
DNI Jay Clayton tied an NSA outage to patching, which Fox Business linked to a PHP flaw; he saw no sign of a coordinated attack
FAA ground stop; Fox News reported a faulty router caused it. The FAA saw zero evidence of anything AI-related, and Microsoft and Chase blamed software bugs
hosts run Nginx, per Shodan. Four teams, three of them using AI, found a critical flaw in every release since 2015; F5 has shipped fixes
